maya (support): @ben sorry you're seeing truncated streams — can you paste a minimal repro?
ben (customer): running on Vercel Edge runtime, Node target edge, using our TS SDK. stream starts fine but final chunk (closing 'data' event) never arrives, response just ends early. happens after a retry (503 -> retry) 2/3 times.
maya (support): thanks. can you confirm SDK version and any proxy/edge config?
ben (customer): redwood-js-sdk v0.3.1, nextjs 13, vercel runtime edge. no custom proxy. token rotates with our auth service every ~5m.
devon (eng-runtime): 0.3.1 is pretty old — we shipped a streaming edge fix in 0.3.5 and changed how we flush the ReadableStream on retry. can you capture the browser/edge logs and a small fetch snippet?
ben (customer): here's the fetch snippet I used to reproduce:
```
const res = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }, body: JSON.stringify({ prompt }) });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
let done = false;
while (!done) {
  const { value, done: d } = await reader.read();
  if (value) console.log('chunk len', value.byteLength);
  done = d;
}
console.log('stream closed')
```
ben (customer): logs show: chunk len 1024, 1024, 768, then stream closed, but server had one more 512-byte chunk.
maya (support): curious — do you see any 503s in the request history that correspond to a retry?
ben (customer): yes, trace shows: initial 200, then later a 503 on the retry attempt, followed by a 200 that returns truncated body.
devon (eng-runtime): can you also capture the edge logs (Vercel) and any SDK debug logs? enable REDWOOD_SDK_DEBUG=1 environment var. also which fetch polyfill are you using?
ben (customer): using native fetch from edge runtime. attached small trace: 
```
[1728887601] request id=abc123 -> upstream 503, retrying
[1728887602] request id=abc123 retry#1 -> upstream 200, streaming start
[1728887603] streamed 3400 bytes total at server side
[1728887603] client saw 2880 bytes, stream closed
```
li (eng-ml): this looks like a KV-cache + retry edge case where we switch model variants on fallback. if the runtime swaps kernels mid-stream there's a chance the tail buffer isn't flushed to the same connection.
maya (support): @devon any known ReadableStream behavior in edge runtimes that could cause early .read() done=true?
devon (eng-runtime): yes — the spec allows a closed stream after controller.close(); if our retry handler closes the previous controller before piping the final buffered chunk into the new controller, the client will see done=true and miss data. we changed this in 0.3.5 to keep the previous controller open until we drain pending chunks. bug repro relates to SDK's retry handler invoking controller.close() on the old stream.
ben (customer): ahhh makes sense. is there a suggested workaround until we patch?
devon (eng-runtime): two options: 1) pin SDK to v0.3.5+ which includes the fix; 2) as a temporary workaround, set REDWOOD_SDK_RETRY_MODE=off to avoid automated retries in the edge environment (risky for production).
ben (customer): trying v0.3.5 now...
deploy-bot: deploy started for customer-app (branch: fix/edge-stream-triage)
ben (customer): after upgrading to 0.3.6 the repro no longer reproduces in my quick test, final chunk arrives consistently. thanks! :tada:
maya (support): great — @ben can you confirm the patch fixes it for your full load test? we'll keep this thread open for 48h. :eyes:
ben (customer): will run load test and report back by EOD PST.
li (eng-ml): follow-up: adding an integration test to the edge-suite to simulate a retry that returns extra tail chunks. tracking in ENG-3589.
devon (eng-runtime): once ben confirms we'll schedule a backport to the 0.3.x maintenance branch and announce in #eng-releases.
maya (support): marking as triaged for now. thanks everyone! :heart:
